title: Realtime Data Connectivity for AI: Tanmai Gopal

primary.label: Tools, Protocols & Integrations

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on exposing live data and business logic as tools to LLMs via a unified query language protocol and autonomous query planning across multiple sources. Pacha DDN is a developer platform for AI data connectivity, and the use cases focus on data-agent products spanning analytics and enterprise data sources. Pacha DDN is presented as a shipping product with a working live demo, indicating production-stage maturity. Requires basic familiarity with LLMs, SQL, and APIs but remains accessible to a general AI engineering audience. A recorded live conference presentation at AI Engineer World's Fair featuring a live multi-source data demo. All selected evidence anchors are directly quoted from the transcript with grade 'said_in_transcript'.

summary: Tanmai Gopal opens with an existential framing: as AI becomes ubiquitous, we must give AI systems access to the data they need. He identifies a core pain point: LLMs can write code rapidly (a Flappy Bird clone in 30 seconds) but cannot intelligently talk to live data. He illustrates with real-world examples: querying calendar data for one-on-one scheduling, investigating stuck Salesforce deals, cross-referencing support tickets with enterprise customer project data, and checking product availability for one-day delivery. The problem is compounded by security concerns—users are reluctant to connect personal data like calendars to opaque LLM systems. Gopal's solution, Pacha DDN, exposes live data and business logic as a tool to the LLM. A live demo uses a Blockbuster-style movie streaming database, asking the system to write an email to a top customer thanking them and mentioning recently watched movies, successfully pulling data from two to three different sources. Three key technical ideas underpin the approach. First, a unified query language: LLMs already understand SQL semantics (e.g., 'greater than' has clear meaning), unlike opaque API URL parameters, so all data sources—structured, unstructured, and APIs—should be exposed through one query language. Second, an object model for authorization: authorization rules are properties of the data schema and session, independent of where data resides or how it is accessed, enabling consistent security across all access paths. Third, autonomous query planning: rather than hardcoding data retrieval logic, the LLM is prompted to write Python code to fetch and assemble data from multiple sources. Gopal argues that LLMs struggle with certain reasoning tasks (like counting letters in a word) but excel when asked to write code to solve the same problem. He closes with a call to prepare for the 'data Singularity' and invites attendees to visit Hasura's booth.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Problem Statement
sections.summary: Tanmai frames the problem existentially and shares frustrations with LLMs that can generate code but cannot intelligently access live data from calendars, Salesforce, tickets, and product databases. He highlights security concerns with connecting personal data to opaque LLM systems.

sections.title: Solution Overview and Live Demo
sections.summary: Introduces the core idea of exposing live data and business logic as a tool to the LLM. A live demo uses a Blockbuster-style movie database to compose an email to a top customer mentioning recently watched movies, successfully retrieving data from multiple sources.

sections.title: Three Key Ideas for Data Connectivity
sections.summary: Details three technical pillars: (1) a unified query language using SQL semantics that LLMs already understand, (2) an object model for authorization based on data schema and session properties independent of access method, and (3) autonomous LLM-driven query planning via Python code generation rather than hardcoded retrieval logic.

sections.title: Conclusion: Data Singularity
sections.summary: Gopal calls for preparation for the 'data Singularity,' invites attendees doing AI, data, or both to visit Hasura's booth, and closes the talk.
